name: University of Groningen
summary: Founded in 1614, a large research university (32,500 students, 26% international) in the student city of Groningen, with a campus in Leeuwarden.

ib.text: The IB Diploma counts as Dutch VWO; no minimum points. Strictest subjects: Maths AA HL and Physics HL (Physics, Astronomy, Applied Physics). An IB taught in English waives the English test.

apply.via: Studielink, then the RUG Progress Portal

dates.label: Numerus fixus: personal details confirmed in Studielink
Application deadline for all other bachelor's
Numerus fixus: final IB results proving entry requirements due

programmes.name: American Studies
programmes.about: The United States from many angles at once: its politics, history, literature, popular culture, race relations and religions, and its ties with the rest of the Americas. Taught in small seminars.
programmes.overview: First-year courses include The Americas, Theories of Culture, American Politics, a course on how identities are mediated in stories and one on Latin American and Canadian literature, taught in seminars with close contact with faculty. You write papers and also produce TED talks, editorials, exhibits and apps, and practise writing and speaking in American Studies in Practice. In year two you choose among a Media specialisation, Global USA and changing special topics, and you can spend a semester at a partner university in the United States, take a minor, and write a BA thesis. Graduates work in journalism, banking, culture, government and communications, or move on to master programmes such as Euroculture or Digital Humanities.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Applied Mathematics
programmes.about: Using mathematics to model and simulate real systems, from vehicle dynamics to energy networks, combining proofs with programming and simulation. The first year is shared with Mathematics, so you can still switch after it.
programmes.overview: The first year covers analysis, calculus, linear algebra, linear systems, probability, graph theory, mechanics and relativity for mathematicians, and scientific programming, shared with the Mathematics degree so you can still switch. You learn to formulate and analyse abstract models of real systems, for example simulating the dynamics of a bicycle with numerical methods and code, and complete a research project in the final year. In years two and three you specialise in Numerical Mathematics or Systems, Control and Optimization, and an optional study period abroad is available. Graduates go on to the Applied Mathematics master, research and PhD positions, research institutes, consulting, finance and industry, or teaching.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Applied Physics
programmes.about: Physics aimed at technology: the fundamentals plus design, nanotechnology, new materials and control engineering, for work in energy, medical technology and materials. Taught next to Physics, so you need not choose between them straight away.
programmes.overview: The first year covers calculus, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, electricity and magnetism, mathematical physics, computational methods, two physics laboratory courses and a course on the physics of modern technology. The programme stays deliberately broad, so you can postpone specialising until year two, and it is tied to research institutes for advanced materials, particle physics, energy and sustainability, and astronomy. An optional exchange semester abroad is possible, and the study association arranges company visits. Graduates work as consultants, researchers, technical innovators and analysts in industry, research institutes such as TNO, or banking and management consulting, or continue to a master in Applied Physics or Nanoscience.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Art History
programmes.about: Visual art, architecture, cities and landscapes studied together and in their environmental context, mixing historical, theoretical and practice-based courses, with an excursion abroad to a city such as Berlin, London or Florence.
programmes.overview: Year one is a survey from Classical Antiquity to the present, with visual analysis, iconography, materials and techniques, garden heritage, and art and architecture since 1750; year two adds contemporary art, architectural theory, the Italian Renaissance and landscape design. Fridays are usually reserved for excursions, within the Netherlands and to cities such as Berlin, London, Florence and Vienna, and a practice lab and a thesis complete the training. You can specialise in Modern & Contemporary Art, Early Modern Art, Architecture & Urbanism, or Landscape History. Graduates work in museums, heritage management, journalism, publishing and teaching, or continue to a master such as Curatorial Studies.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Artificial Intelligence
programmes.about: How intelligence works in people and machines, combining machine learning, programming, cognitive psychology, neuroscience, linguistics and philosophy. Specialise in computational neuroscience, hybrid intelligence, language and AI, machine learning or robotics.
programmes.overview: Year one includes introductions to AI, neuroscience and logic, imperative programming, algorithms and data structures, cognitive psychology, general linguistics, autonomous systems, calculus, linear algebra and statistics. You work on weekly assignments and real-world projects in international teams, and finish with a bachelor project under a researcher. You choose a specialisation from Computational Neuroscience, Hybrid Intelligence, Language and AI, Machine Learning and Robotics, and a period abroad is optional. Graduates work as machine learning engineers, data scientists, robotics engineers or software developers in software companies, research institutions, hospitals and banks, or continue to a master in Computational Cognitive Science or AI.
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; in Studielink pick the option without the "Numerus fixus" label.

programmes.name: Arts, Culture and Media
programmes.about: Film, music or theatre (with literature or visual arts as a possible second art form) studied in depth, with how art is made, funded and received; choose a framework in arts policy and cultural entrepreneurship or in analysis and criticism.
programmes.overview: Year one covers audiovisual arts, the role of the arts in culture and the sociology of the arts, and you choose a main discipline of film, music or theatre, with literature or visual arts as a second art form. Later years deepen your art form and its philosophical and theoretical grounding, in seminars, group projects, a theatre project shown in local venues and visits to productions and festivals in Groningen. You choose between Arts Policy and Cultural Entrepreneurship or Analysis and Criticism, and the fifth semester can be a career minor, a pre-master or time abroad. Graduates work in theatre companies, concert halls, museums, publishing and media, or continue to master programmes such as Arts in Society or Film and Contemporary Audiovisual Media.
programmes.ib: Apply for the English track; a Dutch track also exists.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Astronomy
programmes.about: Stars, galaxies, planetary systems and cosmology on a solid base of physics and mathematics, with the university's own observatory and links to the SRON and ASTRON space and radio astronomy institutes. You can switch to Physics or Mathematics in year one.
programmes.overview: Year one rests on calculus, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, electricity and magnetism, mathematical physics and programming, with Introduction to Astronomy and Observational Astronomy, which uses the university's own observatory. Year two adds quantum physics, thermodynamics, waves and optics, and courses on the physics of stars, galaxies and radiative processes, taught through lectures and tutorials. In year three you carry out a research project in a research group and can choose a general astronomy minor or one on instrumentation and informatics. The programme links to the ASTRON and SRON institutes. Graduates go on to PhD research, technology roles with satellite and telescope companies, or business positions such as strategy and risk assessment.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Biology
programmes.about: Living systems from molecules to ecosystems, combined with maths, physics and chemistry. A broad first semester, then a major in ecology and evolution, molecular life sciences, behaviour and neurosciences, or biomedical sciences (partly at the UMCG hospital).
programmes.overview: The first year covers cell and molecular biology, biostatistics, genetics, ecology and evolution, microbiology, physiology and behavioural neuroscience, taught in intensive three-week courses with practicals, fieldwork and independent study. You then choose a major in Ecology and Evolution, Molecular Life Sciences, Behaviour and Neurosciences, or Biomedical Sciences, the last partly at the University Medical Center Groningen. A third-year minor semester can be spent abroad, and you complete a research project and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as researchers, environmental advisors, ecologists, policy advisors, science communicators or teachers, or continue to a master in fields such as marine biology or neurosciences.
programmes.ib: Biology HL, plus Physics, Chemistry and Maths (AA SL/HL or AI HL); all four subjects are required.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Biomedical Engineering
programmes.about: Engineering for healthcare: medical imaging, robotics, biomaterials and tissue engineering, on problems such as longer-lasting heart valves or automated MRI analysis. Run with the University Medical Center Groningen, where some courses are taught.
programmes.overview: You combine mathematics, physics, biology and engineering, with first-year courses in anatomy and physiology, cell biology, microbiology, materials science, biomaterials, biomechanics and the design of biomedical products. Projects tackle problems such as designing artificial heart valves or MRI analysis software, backed by physics, microbiology and imaging labs. Some courses are taught by medical experts at the University Medical Center Groningen, and you can take a minor in Biomaterials Science and Engineering, Medical Device Design or Medical Imaging before a bachelor research project. Most graduates continue to the Biomedical Engineering master, leading to roles in medical device R&D, PhD research, hospitals, certification bodies and start-ups.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL, plus Physics and Chemistry with at least one of the two at HL. Biology recommended.

needs.note: Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).
Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).

programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Chemical Engineering
programmes.about: Designing and optimising large-scale processes for fuels, food, medicines and materials, through thermodynamics, transport phenomena and reactor engineering. Most of year one is shared with Chemistry, and you can switch between the two during that year.
programmes.overview: Year one is shared with Chemistry, covering mathematics for chemistry, organic, physical and inorganic chemistry, spectroscopy and an introduction to chemical engineering. Year two turns to thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactors, separation processes, polymer chemistry and green chemistry. Laboratory practicals run throughout, with a process design project and a bachelor research project carried out with industry partners, and a semester abroad is optional. The programme draws on companies such as Shell, BASF and AkzoNobel. Graduates become chemical or energy engineers, product developers or researchers, or continue to a master in Chemical Engineering or Energy & Environmental Sciences.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL, plus Physics and Chemistry with at least one of the two at HL.

needs.note: Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).
Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).

programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Chemistry
programmes.about: Organic, inorganic and physical chemistry with a lot of lab research, then a specialisation in smart materials, chemistry of life, or sustainable chemistry and energy. You can switch to Chemical Engineering during the first year.
programmes.overview: Early courses cover concepts of chemistry, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry, biochemistry, spectroscopy and mathematics for chemistry, combining theory with hands-on work in modern laboratories, including synthesis, analysis and biochemistry labs. You can join staff research projects early on and then specialise in Smart Materials, Chemistry of Life, or Sustainable Chemistry and Energy. The programme is tied to the Stratingh Institute for Chemistry and the Zernike Institute for Advanced Materials, and a semester abroad is possible. Graduates work as industrial or scientific researchers, managers, in commercial roles or as teachers, or continue to a master such as Chemistry, Biomolecular Sciences or Nanoscience.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL, plus Physics and Chemistry with at least one of the two at HL.

needs.note: Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).
Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).

programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Communication and Information Studies
programmes.about: Why communication succeeds or fails, across text, talk, images, digital media and generative AI, drawing on linguistics, psychology, media studies and marketing. You design and test improvements for real cases in corporate, health and intercultural communication.
programmes.overview: Year one looks at how communication works in text, talk and other forms, with courses on persuasion and argumentation, intercultural communication, qualitative research methods and academic English. In year two you apply it in team projects on real cases, with corporate and organisational communication, digital and social media, health communication and quantitative methods. The fifth semester can be a minor, a career minor with an internship, or study abroad, and the degree ends with an independent research thesis. Dutch speakers can follow a Dutch track. Graduates work as communications officers, consultants, editors, press officers, journalists or marketing managers, or continue to a master such as Communication Studies or Digital Humanities.
programmes.ib: Apply for the English track; a Dutch track also exists.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Computing Science
programmes.about: The theory and practice of computing: programming in several languages, algorithms, mathematical foundations, software and systems design and data analysis, with room for creative projects and research in fields such as bioinformatics and astronomy.
programmes.overview: The first year covers programming fundamentals, object-oriented programming, algorithms and data structures in C, computer architecture, networks, logic, discrete structures, calculus, linear algebra and information systems. There is creative freedom in projects and practicals, with quick feedback on programming work, and opportunities for an internship in a research group or company or for study abroad. The programme is linked to research groups in computer architecture, distributed systems, intelligent systems, software engineering and scientific visualisation. Graduates work as software developers, data engineers, cybersecurity experts, machine learning specialists or game developers, or continue to a master in Computing Science or AI.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; in Studielink pick the option without the "Numerus fixus" label.

programmes.name: Data Science and Society
programmes.about: Programming, data analysis and machine learning taught together with the law, ethics and politics of data, with projects for real organisations on the small Leeuwarden campus. In year two you specialise in AI and Society or in Cognitive Technology.
programmes.overview: You study programming in Python, databases and SQL, big data analytics, statistical and machine learning, visualising data and statistical inference alongside science and technology studies, the governance of innovation and human rights in the digital age. Learning is discussion-based, with one-to-one mentoring and field projects for partner organisations such as the Dutch statistics bureau CBS, Datamaran and TEXroad, in Leeuwarden with its DataFryslan initiative. In year two you specialise in AI and Society or in Cognitive Technology, and year three offers study abroad or a minor, plus a bachelor thesis. Graduates become data engineers, data scientists, data analysts, data protection officers or policy advisors.
programmes.ib: Maths AA or AI, SL or HL, with a pass.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027 for September; a February 2027 start has an earlier deadline.
programmes.closesNote: A February start has an earlier deadline

programmes.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
programmes.about: Mathematical modelling of economic and business problems, combining econometrics, operations research, actuarial science and mathematical economics, with a simulation game in which you run a company in all three years.
programmes.overview: The first year builds mathematics (calculus, linear algebra, analysis), probability, programming, finance, microeconomics, operations research modelling and statistical modelling, and year two adds convexity and optimisation, macroeconomics, game theory, econometrics, stochastic and discrete operations research and actuarial courses on life and risk insurance. In all three years you run a company in the EOR Game simulation, working in small groups with personal contact with lecturers. You choose a profile in Econometrics, Operations Research, Actuarial Science or Mathematical Economics, and year three offers a minor or study abroad. Most graduates continue to a master, then work as quantitative analysts, consultants, actuaries or risk managers.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Economics and Business Economics
programmes.about: Economic tools for questions such as inequality, growth and climate impact, with strong data skills. Specialise in Economics, Business Economics, or International Economics and Sustainable Development; year three leaves room for a minor, internship or exchange.
programmes.overview: The first year covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, financial accounting, statistics, data analysis, international economics, finance and investments, the Dutch economy and writing and presenting, and ends with a research project. From year two you choose a profile: Business Economics, Economics, or International Economics and Sustainable Development. Teamwork and real-world data projects are central, with mentor groups, and year three offers a minor, a semester abroad or an internship, plus an empirical bachelor thesis. Graduates work as financial analysts, policy advisors, risk analysts, consultants or researchers, or continue to a master in finance, economics or a related field.
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL. Tracks: Economics, Business Economics, or International Economics and Sustainable Development.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: English Language and Culture
programmes.about: English literature, culture and linguistics from medieval origins to today, across Britain, North America and the wider English-speaking world, taught in small classes; the oldest English programme in the Netherlands.
programmes.overview: Year one includes medieval English literature, an overview of English literatures from Chaucer and Shakespeare to Austen and Atwood, English linguistics and the structure of language in social contexts, and Professional English for academic writing, presentations and debate. Year two adds cognitive aspects of language and identities and ideologies from medieval to modern times, with options such as sociolinguistics, Arthurian studies and early modern literature. Classes are small, a placement and a minor are possible, and you can study at partner universities in the UK and Ireland. About 80 percent continue to a master, and graduates work in publishing, politics, cultural organisations, tourism, communications and education.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: European Languages, Cultures and Politics
programmes.about: Europe's politics, cultures and languages, with intensive study of one major language (German, English, French, Italian, Dutch, Russian, Spanish or Swedish) towards near-native level, and a profile in language, culture or politics from year two.
programmes.overview: The first year introduces European language and society, European culture and literature, and European politics and society, together with progressive language training in your major language: German, English, French, Italian, Dutch, Russian, Spanish or Swedish. Language units are intensive and usually in small groups, and from year two you follow one of three profiles: European Language and Society, European Culture and Literature, or European Politics and Society. Year three includes a minor, which can be a work placement, research or teacher training, or study abroad, and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy officers, communications consultants, journalists, teachers or translators, or continue to a master such as Euroculture.
programmes.ib: German major needs B1–B2 (school-leaving German, EU, under 2 years old); French needs A2 proof; Spanish Plus A2, else Spanish basic; Italian, Russian, Swedish, Dutch from zero.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Global Politics and Sustainability
programmes.about: Climate, biodiversity and energy transitions seen through politics, economics and society, with a specialisation in Planet or Politics and a Living Lab project for outside partners, in a small programme in Leeuwarden. Formerly Global Responsibility & Leadership.
programmes.overview: Year one combines environmental systems and climate science, political and economic analysis, research methods, and the sustainable energy transition and leadership for sustainability. In year two you follow a Planet track on energy futures and resource use or a Politics track on power, inequality and political and economic systems. Teachers act as coaches, and living-lab projects with outside partners, such as Amnesty International and Friesland social organisations, tackle real sustainability challenges. Year three has an exchange, internship or minor and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy advisors, researchers or consultants in government, NGOs and business, or continue to a master such as Political Science or Environmental Sciences.
programmes.ib: Maths AA or AI, SL or HL, with a pass. Selective: a CV and a motivation letter or video, in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Selective: once found eligible, you upload a CV and a motivation letter (max. 500 words) or video (max. 3 min), in English. Apply early: an Early Bird round closes first.
programmes.closesNote: Early Bird 15 Jan; February start: 1 Nov 2026

programmes.name: History
programmes.about: The international track of History: a survey from Antiquity to the present, then political, cultural, economic and social history centred on a world region you choose, ending in your own research and thesis. All classes are in English.
programmes.overview: Year one covers ancient, medieval, early modern and contemporary history, Dutch history in a global setting, historical sources and academic writing, and year two adds modern history, cultural, political and economic and social approaches, historical theory and a region of your choice for deeper study. Lecture courses are combined with working groups, independent research with papers and presentations, and a bachelor thesis. The fifth semester can be a career minor with a placement, study abroad or another minor. Graduates work as policy officers, journalists, museum professionals or educators, or continue to a master such as History and Heritage Consultancy or Euroculture.
programmes.ib: Apply for the English track; a Dutch track also exists.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Human Geography and Planning
programmes.about: Why cities and regions develop differently and how to plan better places, combining economic, cultural and population geography, real estate studies and planning, with statistics taking a large share of the programme.
programmes.overview: You study urbanism and planning, economic, population and rural geography, migration and development, culture and place, governance and physical geography, with statistics, GIS and qualitative and quantitative research methods. Fieldwork takes place every year, and first-year students are paired with senior mentors in small groups. Year three offers an optional internship with, for example, a local government planning department, a semester abroad, and a bachelor project. Graduates work as spatial planning advisors in consultancies, project managers in local government, researchers at housing associations or geography teachers, or continue to one of the specialised master programmes in spatial sciences.
programmes.ib: No subject requirements, but statistics is a big part: a maths level like Dutch VWO Maths A, B or C is expected.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Industrial Engineering and Management
programmes.about: An engineering degree with management: about two-thirds technical courses (maths, physics, chemistry, programming) and one-third business, applied to production, supply chains, logistics and energy systems.
programmes.overview: About two thirds of the programme is technical and one third business: first-year courses include calculus, linear algebra, programming, modelling and simulation, transport phenomena and statistics, together with organisational behaviour, management accounting, industrial marketing and global supply chains. A capstone project on the design of complex systems and a final-year integration project solving concrete problems with companies give practical experience. You specialise in Production Technology and Logistics, Sustainable Process Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering, and can study abroad in the third-year minor. Graduates work as process technologists, product managers or consultants in automotive, chemical, pharmaceutical and energy sectors.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL. Physics is not required but strongly advised.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Information Science
programmes.about: Applied AI, data science and language technology: building and evaluating software that processes large amounts of text and data, with attention to human and societal needs. Taught in English at the Faculty of Arts.
programmes.overview: First-year courses cover language technology, information science, programming from scratch, statistics, data manipulation, machine learning, humane AI in digital societies and web development. Teaching favours group projects over big exams, with real-world data challenges, software development exercises and collaborative co-creative AI work, balanced between theory and practice. Electives lean towards law and IT, business, AI, linguistics and communication, and the fifth semester can be a minor or study abroad before a bachelor thesis project. Graduates work as data scientists, software developers, analytics consultants or content managers, or continue to a master in Information Science or Natural Language Processing.
programmes.ib: Maths at Dutch VWO A/B level, judged from course descriptions (else an entrance exam). The page also asks internationals for Dutch at B2 (NT2).

needs.note: Judged from your course descriptions; if short, you sit an entrance exam.

programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: International and European Law
programmes.about: International, European and comparative law rather than one national legal system, with an optional Technology Law track from year two and a semester abroad for every student. It does not qualify you to practise law in the Netherlands.
programmes.overview: Year one covers legal English and research skills, Dutch law as an example of legal skills, criminal law, legal history, contract and tort law, and an introduction to international and European law; year two adds comparative constitutional law, technology law, EU law, property law, law, power and politics and public international law. From year two you choose International and European Law or Technology Law. Everyone spends a semester abroad at a partner university in year three and writes a bachelor thesis. Almost all graduates continue to a master, and they work as diplomats, policy advisors, NGO and UN specialists or compliance officers.
programmes.ib: Compulsory online matching. English test can be waived if your IB school teaches only in English, or with English A or English B HL (B SL: a 5 and 35 points).
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective, but the online matching activity is compulsory (its advice is not binding); skip it and your registration is blocked. Apply and upload by 1 May 2027.

programmes.name: International Business
programmes.about: International business seen through management, finance, marketing, ethics, sociology, psychology and economics, with real company cases and a third year for exchange, an internship or a minor. About 40% of students come from abroad.
programmes.overview: Year one covers global supply chain management, international business, financial accounting, organisational behaviour, economics, international marketing, statistics and international trade, and year two adds digital transformation, finance, ethics, cross-cultural management, global political economy and international business law. You work on real company cases, team projects and discussion seminars with guest speakers. In year three you choose a semester abroad, an internship or a minor such as data analytics, finance or innovation and entrepreneurship. Graduates work as export managers, international marketers, sales or product managers, or analysts, or continue to a master in International Business and Management, Finance or Marketing.
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus, 550 places: apply by 15 January 2027; an online Fit & Benchmark activity ranks applicants. Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL.
programmes.selectionNote: 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published: an online Fit & Benchmark activity (videos, readings, questions) ranks everyone; CV and grades do not count.

programmes.name: International Relations and International Organization
programmes.about: International politics studied through history, economics, law and international organisations, plus training in a modern foreign language and a minor of your choice, in a programme running for three decades.
programmes.overview: First-year modules include Economics for Public Policy, the historical foundations of modern IR, Introduction to International Relations, contemporary global history, political systems of the world and theories for analysing IR; year two covers security studies, EU governance, global political economy, international law and research methods. Assignments are varied, from essays and research papers to video production and group presentations, with a language course along the way. You choose from about ten specialisation themes, take a minor in year three and write a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy advisors, lobbyists, journalists and researchers in governments, NGOs and international organisations, or continue to a master such as International Security.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
programmes.about: University College Groningen's small liberal arts programme: explore several disciplines, then major in Humanities, Sciences or Social Sciences, with team projects for outside partners and much class discussion. Starts in September or February.
programmes.overview: The first years combine academic and professional skills, an introduction to academic research and core electives on the challenges of modern society, with research and methodology courses in the sciences, social sciences or humanities. Seminars are small and interactive, and you work in teams on real-world projects, often with outside partners, with a capstone project each year and a bachelor thesis. You major in Sciences, Social Sciences or Humanities, and choose a minor, an exchange abroad or an internship; a double degree track with Ca' Foscari University in Venice is available. About 84 percent of graduates continue to a master, in fields such as psychology, medicine or international relations.
programmes.ib: Selective (University College Groningen): an eligibility check, then a motivation video decides.
programmes.selectionNote: Selective, not numerus fixus: an eligibility check first, then your motivation video decides. Apply early: an Early Bird round closes before the final deadline.
programmes.closesNote: Early Bird 15 Jan; February start: 1 Nov 2026

programmes.name: Life Science and Technology
programmes.about: Life at the molecular scale, combining biology, chemistry, physics and pharmacology: drug design, cellular imaging and bioinformatics, with lab work from year one. Two broad years come before you specialise.
programmes.overview: Year one includes biochemistry, biophysics, calculus, mammalian cell biology, optics, organic chemistry, pharmaceutical analysis, physiology, programming for life sciences and thermodynamics, and year two adds inorganic chemistry, spectroscopy and microbiology. Practical lab courses run from the first year, and you finish with a research project in your area of specialisation, chosen in year three from pharmaceutical sciences, biology, chemistry or physics. The programme links to four research institutes, including those for biomolecular sciences, chemistry, advanced materials and pharmacy. Graduates typically continue to a master such as Biomolecular Sciences or Medical Pharmaceutical Sciences, leading to research, biomedical engineering, product development or teaching.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL, plus Physics and Chemistry with at least one of the two at HL.

needs.note: Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).
Physics or Chemistry must be HL (at least one of the two).

programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Mathematics
programmes.about: Pure mathematics in depth: algebra, topology, analysis, probability, number theory and dynamical systems, with a focus on rigorous proof. The first year is shared with Applied Mathematics, so you can switch without delay.
programmes.overview: The shared first year covers analysis, linear algebra, sets and numbers, probability, graph theory, linear systems, mechanics and relativity for mathematicians, and scientific programming, so you can still switch to Applied Mathematics. Later years add statistics, group theory, partial differential equations, complex analysis, functional analysis and numerical mathematics, with flexible electives in algebra, topology, probability and dynamical systems. You complete a first-year project, a research project and a bachelor thesis, and a double degree with Physics is possible. The degree leads to the Mathematics master and to work as a researcher, consultant, analyst or teacher, with employers such as Shell, Philips and ABN Amro.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Media Studies
programmes.about: The social and informative role of media, from print and television to platforms and search engines, studied comparatively in their political, economic and cultural contexts with social-science methods, plus professional skills for media work.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces media studies, media and everyday life, how media past, present and future connect, and theories of audiences and uses, alongside professional writing and academic skills; year two covers representations in media, analysing media texts, production and use, and a research seminar. You choose a profile in Visual Culture, Cultural Industries, Digital Cultures, Journalism Studies, or Politics and Global Citizenship. A minor can be a career minor with an internship, or you can study abroad, and the degree ends with a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as strategy consultants, social media analysts, policy advisors, content producers and PR professionals, or continue to a master such as Journalism.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Physics
programmes.about: Mechanics, electromagnetism and quantum physics with plenty of lab work, then a specialisation in biophysics and medical physics, energy and environmental physics, nanophysics, particle physics, or physics education.
programmes.overview: The first year covers calculus, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, electricity and magnetism, mathematical physics, computational methods and two physics laboratory courses, with introductory electives such as astronomy, medical physics, nanophysics and quantum topics. You gain hands-on lab experience, learn to turn complex theory into practical solutions, and complete a bachelor research project, with study abroad as an option. Specialisations include Nanophysics, Particle Physics, Energy & Environmental Physics, Biophysics & Medical Physics and physics education, linked to research institutes for advanced materials, particle physics and energy. Graduates continue to a master such as Physics or Nanoscience and work in research, industry, consultancy, analytics or teaching.
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May 2027; no matching needed if you apply by then.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.about: All core areas of psychology, from the brain to society, with a strong grounding in statistics and research methods and skills training in small mentor-led groups. The English track has the same content as the Dutch one.
programmes.overview: The first years cover biological, developmental, cognitive, social and cross-cultural psychology, personality and individual differences, the history of psychology, research methods and statistics, and professional methods such as test administration. You learn in small mentor-led groups, with research practicals in which you design and present studies, role-play exercises and a bachelor thesis on your own research project in year three. Professional areas include work and organisational psychology, clinical psychology and clinical neuropsychology, and you can study abroad through a minor or join the honours college. Graduates continue to a psychology master or one in neurosciences, and work as psychologists, market researchers or organisational consultants.
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus, 250 places (English track): apply by 15 January 2027; a selection test plus a lottery rank applicants. No subject requirements; maths strongly advised.
programmes.selectionNote: Online selection test on 6 Mar 2027 (set reading and a lecture, three multiple-choice tests) counts 50%, a lottery 50%. Ranking numbers 15 Apr.

programmes.name: Religious Studies
programmes.about: How religion shapes lives and societies, studied through history, anthropology, sociology, psychology, political science and philosophy, on topics such as migration, radicalisation and climate, at a non-denominational faculty.
programmes.overview: You begin with the major world religions, Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Buddhism and Hinduism, the concepts and methods of the study of religion, the anthropology, psychology, sociology and philosophy of religion, and religion in South Asia. Assessment leans on written assignments and research papers, year two includes Rituals in Theory and Practice, and year three has a thesis seminar and an independent bachelor thesis; Quranic Arabic is optional. A minor can be Spiritual Care, teacher training or study at another faculty, and an internship or exchange is possible. Graduates work in care, policy and management, education, church, culture and media, or continue to a master such as Religion, Conflict and Globalization.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

programmes.name: Spatial Planning and Design
programmes.about: Planning and designing living environments: physical and institutional design, water management, infrastructure, environmental planning and spatial software, with excursions to see real projects and a closing research project.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces the power of design, urbanism and planning, economic geography, research skills, statistics and GIS, with a Spatial Design Atelier for studio work; year two covers infrastructure and mobility, water management, governance dynamics, physical geography and research methods. Learning happens in studios, on excursions to see spatial projects in real life, in virtual environments and in team projects that reflect professional practice, ending with a bachelor thesis. Year three leaves room for a minor or exchange, and an honours college is available. Graduates work in policy for spatial planning, environment and mobility, in consulting and real estate development, or continue to one of 13 master programmes in spatial sciences.
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.selectionNote: Not selective: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May 2027; matching is optional and its advice is not binding.

notes: You must earn at least 45 of the 60 first-year credits to continue (binding study advice); Liberal Arts and Sciences and Global Politics and Sustainability ask for all 60.
Applicants with a non-Dutch diploma, IB included, pay a non-refundable €100 application fee, once per year.
Early Bird: a complete application between 1 October and 28 February to most programmes (not the numerus fixus ones) gets a decision within 15 working days.
